It is the kind of seam the Torah leaves visible, and no note can close it honestly.

  • v25 the woman whose flow does not stop — a chronic condition, treated at length and with no stigma attached beyond the same rules that apply to everyone else in the chapter. This is the law the woman in the crowd at Mark 5:25 has been living under: the Greek says she was in a flow of blood twelve years, using the word the Greek Old Testament uses for zov. What she then does is reach through a crowd and take hold of a man's cloak (5:27) — and by vv21–27 here, touching is exactly what transmits. In Mark the transmission runs the other way.

  • v31 the reason, finally — thirty verses of beds and seats and washing, and then the point: so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling My dwelling, which is among them. The rules are not about hygiene and not about morality. They exist because of where God has chosen to live. Mishkani, My dwelling, is the word from Exodus 25:9, and the last three words of the verse are the whole problem — asher be-tokham, which is among them. Something holy has been set down in the middle of an ordinary camp full of bodies, and the rest follows from that.

speech.text: Leviticus 15
A Man with a Discharge
And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
And this is his uncleanness in his discharge: whether his body runs with the discharge or his body is stopped up from the discharge, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed the man with the discharge lies on is unclean, and everything he sits on is unclean.
And anyone who touches his bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whoever sits on anything the man with the discharge sat on shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And if the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And anything he rides on is unclean.
And anyone who touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening; and whoever carries those things shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And anyone the man with the discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And an earthen vessel the man with the discharge touches shall be broken, and every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water.
And when the man with the discharge becomes clean of his discharge, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh running water, and he is clean.
And on the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
And the priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for his discharge.
Emissions
And when a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water, and be unclean until evening.
And every garment and every hide with semen on it shall be washed in water, and be unclean until evening.
And a woman a man lies with, with an emission of semen — they shall both bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
A Woman's Flow
And when a woman has a discharge, and the discharge in her body is blood, she shall be in her monthly separation seven days, and anyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.
And everything she lies on in her separation is unclean, and everything she sits on is unclean.
And anyone who touches her bed shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And anyone who touches anything she sits on shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And if it is on the bed, or on whatever she is sitting on, when he touches it, he shall be unclean until evening.
And if a man does lie with her and her separation comes on him, he shall be unclean seven days, and every bed he lies on shall be unclean.
A Flow Out of Season

And when a woman's flow of blood runs many days at a time that is not her monthly separation, or when it runs past her separation, all the days of her unclean flow she shall be as in the days of her separation. She is unclean.
Every bed she lies on all the days of her flow shall be to her like the bed of her separation, and everything she sits on shall be unclean, like the uncleanness of her separation.
And anyone who touches them shall be unclean, and shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And when she becomes clean of her flow, she shall count seven days for herself, and after that she is clean.
And on the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And the priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean flow.
Why This Matters
And you shall keep the sons of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling My dwelling, which is among them."
This is the instruction for the man with a discharge, and for the man who has an emission of semen and is unclean by it,
and for the woman who is unwell in her separation, and for anyone with a discharge, male or female, and for a man who lies with an unclean woman.

chapters.title: Once a Year
chapters.html:
Leviticus 16

After the Death of the Two Sons

1And the LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, when they came near before the LORD and died.

2And the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron your brother, that he is not to come at just any time into the holy place inside the veil, in front of the cover that is on the ark, or he will die — because I appear in the cloud over the cover.

3With this Aaron shall come into the holy place: with a bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

4He shall put on a holy linen tunic, and linen undergarments shall be on his body, and he shall tie a linen sash around him and wind a linen turban on his head. These are holy garments. And he shall bathe his body in water and put them on.

5And from the congregation of the sons of Israel he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.

The Two Goats

6And Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering that is his own, and make atonement for himself and for his household.

7And he shall take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

8And Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats: one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.

9And Aaron shall present the goat on which the lot for the LORD fell, and make it a sin offering.

10And the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell shall be set alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it, to send it away to Azazel into the wilderness.

Inside the Veil

11And Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering that is his own, and make atonement for himself and for his household, and he shall slaughter the bull of the sin offering that is his own.

12And he shall take a fire pan full of coals of fire from the altar before the LORD, and his two hands full of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them inside the veil.

13And he shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of the incense shall cover the cover that is over the Testimony, so that he does not die.

14And he shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the cover, on the east side; and in front of the cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger.

15And he shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood inside the veil, and do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the cover and in front of the cover.

16And he shall make atonement for the holy place because of the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel and because of their rebellions, for all their sins. And so he shall do for the tent of meeting, which dwells with them in the middle of their uncleannesses.

17And no one at all shall be in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place, until he comes out. And he shall make atonement for himself and for his household and for the whole assembly of Israel.

18And he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it, and take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar all around.

19And he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it and set it apart from the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel.

The Goat That Goes Away

20And when he has finished making atonement for the holy place and the tent of meeting and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

21And Aaron shall lean both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the guilt of the sons of Israel and all their rebellions, for all their sins, and put them on the head of the goat, and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for it.

22And the goat shall carry on itself all their guilt to a land cut off; and he shall send the goat away in the wilderness.

23And Aaron shall come into the tent of meeting and take off the linen garments he put on when he went into the holy place, and leave them there.

24And he shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his garments, and come out and make his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.

25And the fat of the sin offering he shall turn into smoke on the altar.

26And the one who sends the goat away to Azazel shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may come into the camp.

27And the bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall be carried outside the camp, and their hides and their flesh and their dung shall be burned in the fire.

28And the one who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and after that he may come into the camp.

Once a Year

29And this shall be a lasting statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month, you shall afflict yourselves and do no work at all — neither the native nor the foreigner living among you —

30because on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you. You shall be clean before the LORD from all your sins.

31It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves. It is a lasting statute.

32And the priest who is anointed and whose hand is filled to serve as priest in place of his father shall make the atonement, and he shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments,

33and make atonement for the most holy place; and for the tent of meeting and for the altar he shall make atonement; and for the priests and for all the people of the assembly he shall make atonement.

34And this shall be a lasting statute for you, to make atonement for the sons of Israel for all their sins once a year." And he did as the LORD commanded Moses.

Notes

  • v1 where this chapter is anchored — the greatest day in Israel's calendar is dated, in its first sentence, by a funeral. After the death of Aaron's two sons, when they came near before the LORD and died. Chapter 10 left that event without an explanation and Aaron without an answer. What arrives six chapters later is not an explanation but a procedure: this is how a man goes in there and comes out alive.

  • v4 the clothes he does not wear — Exodus 28 spends a chapter on gold, blue, purple, crimson, the breastpiece with twelve stones, the golden plate reading Holy to the LORD. On the one day of the year the high priest enters the innermost room, he takes all of it off and dresses in plain linen — tunic, undergarments, sash, turban, nothing else. The text still calls them holy garments. He goes in looking like nobody.

  • v8 "Azazel" — la-azazel, and nobody knows what it means. The word occurs four times in the Hebrew Bible, all of them in this chapter, and nowhere else. Three readings have been argued for centuries: that it is a compound of ez, goat, and azal, to go away — the source of English scapegoat, coined by Tyndale; that it is an abstract noun meaning utter removal; or that it is a name. The grammar of this verse leans to the third, because of the parallel it sets up — one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel — where the matching term is a person. The text says no more than that, and neither can anyone else.

  • vv8–10 what the lot decides — two goats, identical, bought by the same congregation for the same purpose. One is killed and its blood carried into the holiest room in the world; the other is stood up alive, loaded, and walked out into the desert. Nothing about either animal chooses which. A lot is cast, and that is the whole of the difference between them.

  • v13 the cloud he hides behind — v2 says God appears in the cloud over the cover, and v13 has the high priest raise a cloud of incense to cover that same cover, so that he does not die. The smoke is not decoration and not atmosphere; it is a screen. The one man permitted into the room goes in and immediately obscures his own view of it.

  • v16 "which dwells with them in the middle of their uncleannesses" — this is what the last six chapters were building toward. The tent is not a clean place set apart from a dirty camp; it is a holy thing sitting in the middle of ordinary human mess, and 15:31 already said the risk that creates. The atonement in this chapter is made for the building before it is made for anybody in it. The sanctuary itself needs cleaning, and what has dirtied it is everyone living around it.

  • v17 "no one at all" — ve-khol adam lo yihyeh, and adam is the whole human race. Not an assistant, not another priest. For the length of this rite the most populous building in the camp holds one man, and the text pauses to say so.

  • v21 "confess over it" — hitvaddah, from yadah, the verb that first appeared at 5:5 where an ordinary Israelite had to say out loud what he had done, and which also gives the thanksgiving offering its name at 7:12. Here it reaches its largest form: one man, hands on a goat's head, saying the wrongs of an entire nation aloud. The words are not recorded.

  • v21 "both his hands" — the written consonants say his hand, singular; the reading tradition says his hands. Leviticus has five such places, and the other one where Aaron's hand is at issue is 9:22, where he lifts it to bless the people. Both are his hands on or toward Israel, and in both the tradition reads two where the letters say one. Note also that everywhere else in Leviticus one hand is leaned on an animal's head (1:4, 4:4). This is the only sacrifice that takes both.

  • v22 "a land cut off" — erets gezerah, from gazar, to cut. The noun turns up otherwise only in Ezekiel's temple plan, where it names a separated area. So the goat goes to a cut-off land, which is what the wilderness is, and the phrase occurs once in this sense. The animal is not killed and is not an offering. It is transport.

  • vv7, 10, 21–22 and 14:7 — two chapters ago a man returning from outside the camp had two birds taken: one killed over running water, one dipped in its blood and released into open country. Here it is two goats: one killed, one released into the wilderness. The same verb carries both, shillach, to send off, and the same logic — something dies, and something else walks away carrying what was wrong, and is never mentioned again.

  • v29 "you shall afflict yourselves" — te'annu et nafshoteikhem, you shall afflict your souls, and nefesh is the throat and the appetite as much as the inner life. The Torah does not use the word fast here or anywhere in this chapter. What is commanded is a day of doing without, undefined, and the tradition that made it a fast had to read the definition out of this phrase. What the verse does say plainly is who it binds: the native and the foreigner living among them, in the same clause.

  • v34 "once a year" — achat ba-shanah, the last three words before the chapter closes. Everything else in Leviticus runs daily, or when someone sins, or when a woman gives birth, or when a mark appears. This happens once, on a fixed date, whether or not anything has gone wrong — the only rite in the book scheduled by the calendar rather than by an event.

chapters.title: The Life Is in the Blood
chapters.html:
Leviticus 17

Nowhere Else to Kill It

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded:

3Any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a sheep or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,

4and has not brought it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the dwelling of the LORD — blood shall be counted against that man. He has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people.

5This is so that the sons of Israel will bring their sacrifices, which they have been sacrificing out in the open field, and bring them to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the LORD.

6And the priest shall dash the blood against the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and turn the fat into smoke as a soothing aroma to the LORD.

7And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat-spirits they have been whoring after. This shall be a lasting statute for them through their generations.

8And say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners living among them, who offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice

9and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to make it for the LORD — that man shall be cut off from his people.

The Life Is in the Blood

10And any man of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners living among them, who eats any blood — I will set My face against the person who eats the blood, and cut that person off from among his people.

11Because the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives; because it is the blood that makes atonement by the life.

12That is why I have said to the sons of Israel: None of you shall eat blood, and the foreigner living among you shall not eat blood.

13And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the foreigners living among them, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

14Because the life of all flesh — its blood is its life. And I said to the sons of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone who eats it shall be cut off.

15And any person, native or foreigner, who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and then he is clean.

16But if he does not wash them and does not bathe his body, he bears his guilt."

Notes

  • v4 "He has shed blood" — dam shafakh, and it is the language of murder. Genesis 9:6: one who sheds the blood of the human, by the human his blood shall be shed — the same verb with the same noun. A man who butchers his own ox in the wrong place is described in the vocabulary reserved for killing a person. The verb before it is yechashev, shall be counted, the accounting word from 7:18 and from Genesis 15:6: something is entered against his name.

  • v7 "the goat-spirits" — se'irim, hairy ones, the ordinary Hebrew word for he-goats, here plural with the article and clearly meaning something that can be sacrificed to. And it is the same word, in the same form, as the two goats of the previous chapter (16:8). One chapter after the Day of Atonement assigns two se'irim by lot, the next forbids sacrificing to the se'irim. Whatever they are — the word is used again of the creatures that dance in Babylon's ruins at Isaiah 13:21 — the text will not say more about them than that Israel has been going to them.

  • v7 "whoring after" — zonim achareihem, from zanah, the plain word for prostitution. It is the Bible's standing metaphor for worshipping anything else, and it is not a polite one: the relationship is marriage and the offense is infidelity, not error. Softening it to going astray removes the only thing the sentence is doing.

  • vv3–9 the point of the restriction — an Israelite may not kill an ox anywhere but at the one door. Not because slaughter is wrong, but because sacrifice in the open field is what they have been doing, and to whom. The law does not argue with the practice; it moves it. Everything gets brought to one place where a priest can see it.

  • v11 "the life of the flesh is in the blood" — nefesh ha-basar ba-dam hi, and nefesh is the word English Bibles usually print as soul. It is not a spirit that can leave a body; it is breath, throat, appetite, the living of a living thing — the word used of animals in Genesis 1 before it is ever used of a person. So this sentence is not metaphysics. It is a statement about what blood is: the life itself, in liquid form, which is why it may not be eaten and why it is the one substance that can be put on the altar in place of a life.

  • v11 "makes atonement by the life" — ba-nefesh yekhapper, three words that can be read at least three ways: the blood atones by means of the life in it, or in place of a life, or at the cost of a life. The preposition be carries all three and the verse does not choose. It is the single most quoted sentence in Leviticus and its last clause has never been settled.

  • v13 covering the blood of a hunted animal — a deer or a bird killed out in the hills cannot be brought to the altar, so its blood is poured on the ground and buried. No priest, no altar, nobody watching. The rule reaches the one situation where there is no institution to enforce it, and makes it a matter of what a man does alone on a hillside with a spade.

  • vv8, 10, 12, 13, 15 "the foreigner" — ger, and the chapter names him in every single paragraph, five times in sixteen verses. The blood law is one of the few in Leviticus that binds the non-Israelite exactly as it binds the native. What is at stake here is not identity; it is the ground everyone is standing on.

  • v10 "I will set My face against" — ve-natatti panai, and God stops speaking through a procedure and speaks in the first person about an individual. Everywhere else the penalty is he shall be cut off, passive, with nobody named as doing the cutting. Here the sentence names Him twice over: I will set My face, and I will cut that person off.

chapters.title: Do Not Uncover
chapters.html:
Leviticus 18

Not Like Egypt, Not Like Canaan

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: I am the LORD your God.

3You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived; and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; and you shall not walk in their statutes.

4You shall do My judgments and keep My statutes, to walk in them. I am the LORD your God.

5And you shall keep My statutes and My judgments, which a person shall do and live by them. I am the LORD.

Whose Nakedness Is Not to Be Uncovered

6No man shall come near to anyone of his own flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.

7You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

8You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. It is your father's nakedness.

9You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born outside.

10You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because their nakedness is your own.

11You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister.

12You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister. She is your father's flesh.

13You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's flesh.

14You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother — you shall not come near his wife. She is your aunt.

15You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

16You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife. It is your brother's nakedness.

17You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are her own flesh. It is depravity.

18And you shall not take a woman together with her sister, as a rival, to uncover her nakedness while she is alive.

And These

19And you shall not come near a woman in the uncleanness of her monthly separation, to uncover her nakedness.

20And you shall not give your emission to your neighbor's wife, to become unclean by her.

21And you shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech; and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

22And you shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is detestable.

23And you shall not give your emission to any animal, to become unclean by it; and a woman shall not stand in front of an animal to mate with it. It is a mixing.

What the Land Does

24Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these, because by all of these the nations I am driving out before you have made themselves unclean.

25And the land became unclean, and I called its guilt to account upon it, and the land vomited out those living in it.

26But you shall keep My statutes and My judgments, and shall not do any of these detestable things — neither the native nor the foreigner living among you —

27because the people of the land who were before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.

28And the land will not vomit you out when you make it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.

29Because anyone who does any of these detestable things — the people who do them shall be cut off from among their people.

30And you shall keep My charge, not to do any of the detestable statutes that were done before you, and not to make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."

Notes

  • v6 "uncover nakedness" — gallot ervah, and the phrase runs through the chapter twenty-four times, so this rendering keeps it identical every time the Hebrew repeats it. Ervah is exposure, the state of being uncovered, and the idiom is a euphemism for sexual relations — Hebrew names the act by naming the shame of being seen. The chapter is built out of one sentence said over and over with the relative changed, which is why it reads like a list rather than an argument.

  • v6 "his own flesh" — she'er besaro, and she'er means both flesh and a blood relative, with no line drawn between the senses. The chapter uses it as its whole principle: these people are not other people, they are you. Verse 10 makes it explicit about a granddaughter — their nakedness is your own.

  • vv7–8 the father's nakedness — twice the text describes an offense against a woman as an offense against a man: the father's wife is your father's nakedness (v8), the brother's wife is your brother's nakedness (v16). The women in those two verses are not blood relatives at all. What the formula tracks in these cases is the marriage, not the bloodline, and it says so by naming the husband.

  • v18 "a woman together with her sister" — ishah el achotah, and this is the hardest verse in the chapter to be sure of. The phrase occurs in seven other places in the Hebrew Bible and in every one of them it is a fixed idiom meaning one to another, used of things: the curtains of the tabernacle coupled one to another (Exodus 26:3, 5, 6), the frames (26:17), the wings of the living creatures touching one another (Ezekiel 1:9, 23; 3:13). Not one of them is about a woman. So this verse can be read as forbidding marriage to a wife's sister — which is what Jacob did, and the word litsror, as a rival, points that way — or as forbidding taking one woman in addition to another at all. The two readings produce two different laws, and the Hebrew supports both.

  • v21 the one prohibition that is not sexual — le-ha'avir la-Molekh, to make pass over to Molech, dropped without transition into the middle of a list about relatives. The verb is avar, to cross over; what the passing consists of is not stated here, though 20:14 and later books use fire. And the sentence that follows it is about speech: you shall not profane the name of your God. Nothing in the chapter explains why this belongs here.

  • v22 "as one lies with a woman" — mishkevei ishah, and the noun is plural: the lyings of a woman. The same plural appears in the parallel at 20:13 and nowhere else in the Bible, and what the plural is doing has never been settled. The verse ends with to'evah, the word Genesis uses for Egyptians eating with Hebrews (43:32) and for shepherds (46:34) — a term for what a given community will not have among it, which is a different kind of word from tamei, unclean, and from sheqets, loathsome, which chapter 11 used of animals.

  • v23 "It is a mixing" — tevel, built on a root for mixing or confounding, and the sense is the running together of things that belong to separate categories. That is the same logic as chapter 11's clean and unclean animals and 19:19's ban on sowing a field with two kinds of seed: the offense named is not cruelty or harm but confusion of kinds. The word occurs in this sense twice in the Bible, here and at 20:12.

  • v23 the woman's clause — the verse addresses a man and then turns and addresses a woman in the same breath, and a woman shall not stand in front of an animal. It is the only sentence in the chapter with a woman as the subject of the prohibition rather than its object. Everything else here is said to men about women.

  • vv25, 28 "the land vomited out" — va-taqi ha-arets, from qi, to vomit, and it is a physical verb used of a sick body. This is the only place in the Torah where the land is the one who acts. Not God expelling the Canaanites, not Israel conquering them: the ground itself is made nauseous and throws off what is on it. And v28 turns it on the audience — the land will not vomit you out — which means the new occupants are being told they are on probation with the same soil.

  • v3 Egypt and Canaan, named together — the chapter opens by naming both the country they came out of and the country they are going into, and forbids the practices of each. It does not say what those practices were. Every account of what Egypt or Canaan actually did comes from somewhere other than this text, and the chapter itself simply says: not like the place behind you, not like the place ahead.

  • v5 "and live by them" — va-chai bahem, four words that became one of the most argued sentences in the Bible: the statutes are given so that a person may live by them. Ezekiel 20 quotes the exact phrase three times in one chapter (vv11, 13, 21) and then, at v25, says God gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not live. The Hebrew here says only what it says, and does not define the living.

chapters.title: Love Your Neighbor as Yourself
chapters.html:
Leviticus 19

You Shall Be Holy

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.

3Each of you shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.

4Do not turn to worthless gods, and do not make cast gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.

5And when you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.

6It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it and on the next day, and what is left over to the third day shall be burned in the fire.

7And if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is foul. It will not be accepted.

8And whoever eats it bears his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person shall be cut off from his people.

What You Leave in the Field

9And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping to the edge of your field, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest.

10And you shall not strip your vineyard bare, and you shall not gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.

How to Treat Each Other

11You shall not steal, and you shall not deal falsely, and you shall not lie to one another.

12And you shall not swear falsely by My name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

13You shall not exploit your neighbor and you shall not rob him. The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight until morning.

14You shall not curse a deaf man, and you shall not put a stumbling block in front of a blind man; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

15You shall not do injustice in judgment. You shall not favor the face of the poor and you shall not defer to the face of the great. In righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.

16You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people. You shall not stand on the blood of your neighbor. I am the LORD.

17You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely correct your neighbor, and not carry guilt because of him.

18You shall not take revenge and you shall not hold a grudge against the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

Mixtures

19You shall keep My statutes. You shall not mate your livestock with a different kind. You shall not sow your field with two kinds. And a garment woven of two kinds shall not come on you.

20And when a man lies with a woman who is a slave promised to another man, and she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an inquiry. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free.

21And he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting — a ram of guilt offering.

22And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD, for the sin he sinned; and he shall be forgiven of the sin he sinned.

23And when you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you shall treat its fruit as forbidden. For three years it shall be forbidden to you. It shall not be eaten.

24And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise offering to the LORD.

25And in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that it will yield more for you. I am the LORD your God.

Marks on the Body

26You shall not eat over the blood. You shall not practice divination and you shall not read omens.

27You shall not round off the edge of your head, and you shall not ruin the edge of your beard.

28And you shall not make a gash in your flesh for the dead, and you shall not put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.

29Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will become a prostitute and the land will be full of depravity.

30You shall keep My sabbaths and fear My sanctuary. I am the LORD.

31Do not turn to ghosts, and do not seek out spirits, to be made unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

The Old, the Foreigner, the Scales

32You shall rise before a gray head and give honor to the face of an old man; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

33And when a foreigner lives with you in your land, you shall not wrong him.

34The foreigner living with you shall be to you as a native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

35You shall not do injustice in judgment — in measuring length, in weight, or in quantity.

36You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

37And you shall keep all My statutes and all My judgments and do them. I am the LORD."

Notes

  • vv18 and 34 the sentence and its twin — ve-ahavta le-re'akha kamokha, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself, is the most quoted line in Leviticus. Sixteen verses later the identical construction is used again, of somebody else: ve-ahavta lo kamokha, and you shall love him as yourself, said of the ger, the foreigner living in your land. Those two verses are the only places in the entire Hebrew Bible where this phrase occurs. The famous one has a twin, and the twin is almost never quoted.

  • v18 "love your neighbor" — the Hebrew does not say love your neighbor the way English does. It is ve-ahavta le-re'akha — love to your neighbor, with a preposition where a direct object would be expected. The construction pushes the sense toward acting lovingly toward someone rather than feeling something about them, and it sits at the end of a paragraph made entirely of actions: do not steal, do not withhold wages overnight, do not curse the deaf, do not take revenge. The command arrives as the summary of a list of things to do and not do.

  • v2 who is being addressed — kol adat benei Yisrael, the whole congregation. Everything up to chapter 16 was spoken to Aaron and his sons; the demand to be holy was a priest's job description. Here the same word is handed to everyone, and the chapter that follows is about wages, scales, gleaning, gossip, and the old man you stand up for.

  • vv9–10 what is left in the field — four things: the edge of the field is not reaped, the dropped stalks are not picked up, the vineyard is not stripped, the fallen grapes are not gathered. The poor and the foreigner are not given anything — they are left something, and they come and take it themselves. This is the law Ruth is working under in Boaz's field, and it is written as a restriction on the owner rather than as a charity.

  • v11 "you shall not lie to one another" — ish ba-amito, the rare word from 6:2, where a man who lies to his amit about a deposit is said to break faith with the LORD. Both verses use the same verb, kachash. Nine of the ten occurrences of amit in the Bible are in Leviticus.

  • v14 the deaf man and the blind man — a curse the deaf man cannot hear, and a stone the blind man cannot see. Both are offenses with no witness and no possibility of retaliation, and the verse ends and you shall fear your God. That formula occurs five times in the Bible, all of them in Leviticus, and every one of the five is attached to a command about someone who cannot fight back: the deaf and blind here, the old man at v32, and at 25:17, 36 and 43 a fellow Israelite in debt or in service.

  • v16 "stand on the blood of your neighbor" — lo ta'amod al dam re'ekha, and what it means is not clear. The preposition can be on, against, beside or over; the phrase might forbid profiting from a neighbor's death, standing by while his life is at risk, or testifying in a capital case. The first half of the verse is about carrying tales, which suggests speech. The Hebrew supports more than one reading and nothing in the verse settles it.

  • v17 "you shall surely correct" — hokheach tokhiach, the verb doubled with itself. Yakhach is to argue a case, set someone right, have it out. The verse pairs it with do not hate your brother in your heart: the alternative to silent hatred is saying something. And the clause that follows, and not carry guilt because of him, makes the silence itself the offense — the one who says nothing ends up holding the guilt.

  • v19 "two kinds" — kil'ayim, and the word for the forbidden cloth is sha'atnez, which occurs twice in the Bible, here and at Deuteronomy 22:11 — where it is defined as wool and linen together. The three bans are one idea: no crossbred animals, no mixed seed, no mixed cloth. It is the logic of chapter 11 applied to farming and weaving, and no reason is given here either.

  • v20 the hardest verse in the chapter — two of its words are effectively unrecoverable. Necherefet, describing the woman's status, occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in this verse; it is usually taken as designated or promised to a man. Biqqoret, the consequence, also occurs once in this form, and has been read as an inquiry, a distinction in punishment, and compensation. What the verse plainly says is that the two are not put to death, and that the reason is her legal condition: because she was not free.

  • v23 "you shall treat its fruit as forbidden" — the Hebrew is va-araltem orlato, you shall foreskin its foreskin, the verb taking its own noun, and the noun is the word for the foreskin removed at circumcision. Young fruit is spoken of as uncircumcised, so the tree is under the same language as a child in its first days. English cannot do the doubling and has nothing to do with the image, so the word here is forbidden and the picture is in this note.

  • v28 "tattoo marks" — ketovet qa'aqa, and qa'aqa occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in this verse. It sits beside a ban on gashing the flesh la-nefesh, for the dead — both are mourning practices, cut into the body. The two halves of the verse belong together, and the ban is not on marking as such but on marking oneself over a death.

  • v36 "an honest ephah and an honest hin" — tsedeq four times in one verse, the noun usually rendered righteousness. Applied to scales it means accurate, and the chapter uses one word for both, so that a correct weight and a right action are the same thing. The verse then attaches the exodus to it: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt — the credential offered for a rule about shopkeeping.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.html:
Leviticus 20

Molech, and the Ones Who Look Away

1And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"And to the sons of Israel you shall say: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the foreigners living in Israel, who gives any of his children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.

3And I Myself will set My face against that man, and cut him off from among his people, because he gave of his children to Molech, to make My sanctuary unclean and to profane My holy name.

4And if the people of the land deliberately shut their eyes to that man when he gives his children to Molech, and do not put him to death,

5then I Myself will set My face against that man and against his family, and cut him off from among their people — him and all who go whoring after him, to whore after Molech.

6And the person who turns to ghosts and to spirits, to whore after them — I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.

7And you shall set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.

8And you shall keep My statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.

The Penalties

9Any man who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father and his mother; his blood is on him.

10And a man who commits adultery with another man's wife — who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife — the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

11And a man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood is on them.

12And a man who lies with his daughter-in-law — both of them shall surely be put to death. They have done a mixing; their blood is on them.

13And a man who lies with a male as one lies with a woman — both of them have done a detestable thing. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on them.

14And a man who takes a woman and her mother — it is depravity. They shall burn him and them in the fire, so that there shall be no depravity among you.

15And a man who gives his emission to an animal shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.

16And a woman who comes near any animal to mate with it — you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on them.

17And a man who takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness — it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off in the sight of the sons of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he bears his guilt.

18And a man who lies with a woman in her sickness and uncovers her nakedness — he has laid bare her source, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.

19And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, because that is laying bare his own flesh. They shall bear their guilt.

20And a man who lies with his uncle's wife has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They shall bear their sin; they shall die childless.

21And a man who takes his brother's wife — it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They shall be childless.

Why You Are Not Like Them

22And you shall keep all My statutes and all My judgments and do them, so that the land I am bringing you into to live in does not vomit you out.

23And you shall not walk in the statutes of the nation I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was sick of them.

24And I said to you: You shall take possession of their ground, and I will give it to you to possess — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

25And you shall separate between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean, and you shall not make yourselves loathsome with any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, which I have separated out for you as unclean.

26And you shall be holy to Me, because I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.

27And a man or a woman who has a ghost or a spirit in them shall surely be put to death. They shall stone them with stones; their blood is on them."

Notes

  • v17 "it is a disgrace" — the Hebrew word is chesed, and this is one of the strangest sentences in the Bible. Chesed is the great covenant word: loyal love, steadfast kindness, the thing God is said to keep for a thousand generations, the word in I desire mercy and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6) and all through the Psalms. Here it names an act punished by being cut off. The spelling is identical and so is the vowel pointing, checked against Hosea 6:6 and Psalm 25:10 — this is not a look-alike. Either one root carried two opposite senses, shame and devotion, or a second root has been swallowed by the first. Nothing in the verse decides it, and the English cannot show the collision, so it is recorded here.

  • v9 "his blood is on him" — damav bo, said six times in this chapter. It is not a statement that the man deserves it. It is a liability formula: the blood is accounted to him and not to the people carrying out the sentence. Israelite law returns to this repeatedly — who is answerable for a death — and the phrase settles the question in three words each time.

  • v4 "deliberately shut their eyes" — ha'alem ya'limu, the verb doubled with itself, which is how Hebrew leans on a word: not a failure to notice but a decision not to see. And v5 makes the consequence fall on the man and his family, and on everyone who followed him. The community that looks away is legislated for in the same breath as the offender.

  • v2 "the people of the land shall stone him" — am ha-arets, and there is no court, no priest and no king in this sentence. Execution here is the work of the general population, and the chapter assigns it to them twice (vv2, 27). What the previous chapter asked of them was leaving grain in a field; this one asks this.

  • chapter 18 and chapter 20 are the same list twice — the first time as prohibitions, the second time with what it costs. Almost every offense in 18 reappears here in the same order, now attached to a penalty, and a few drop out. A reader who wants to know what the Torah thought was worst does not get it from the prohibitions; the weighting is only visible here, where death, being cut off, bearing guilt and dying childless are handed out at different levels.

  • vv20–21 "they shall die childless" — aririm, stripped or bare, used of a person with no descendants. It is a different kind of sentence from the ones around it: nobody executes it and no court is involved. For two of the offenses on this list the punishment is simply that the line ends.

  • v21 "it is an impurity" — niddah, the same word used in chapter 15 for a woman's monthly separation, which is a status and involves no wrongdoing at all. Here it is used of an act. The word does not mean uncleanness of a moral kind in chapter 15 and does seem to in this verse, and the Hebrew uses one noun for both.

  • v23 "I was sick of them" — va-aquts bam, from quts, a verb for loathing, the feeling of being unable to stand something any longer. It is the word used of the Egyptians when the Israelites multiplied (Exodus 1:12). This is God saying it about the previous occupants of Canaan, in the first person, with no legal vocabulary attached.

  • vv24–26 "separated" — badal four times in three verses, and it is the verb of Genesis 1, where God separates light from darkness and waters from waters. The chapter's closing argument is built out of it: I separated you from the peoples (v24), so you separate clean animals from unclean (v25), from things I separated out for you (v25), because I separated you to be Mine (v26). The dietary law and the election of Israel are stated as one act, in one word, four times over. It is the same verb handed to the priesthood at 10:10 and used to close chapter 11.

  • v27 "who has a ghost or a spirit in them" — the Hebrew says ki yihyeh vahem, if there is in them, which describes the medium as containing the thing rather than consulting it. The same two words, ov and yidde'oni, appeared at 19:31 as things not to turn to; here they are inside a person. The text never explains what either is.

speech.text: Leviticus 20
Molech, and the Ones Who Look Away
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

"And to the sons of Israel you shall say: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the foreigners living in Israel, who gives any of his children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
And I Myself will set My face against that man, and cut him off from among his people, because he gave of his children to Molech, to make My sanctuary unclean and to profane My holy name.
And if the people of the land deliberately shut their eyes to that man when he gives his children to Molech, and do not put him to death,
then I Myself will set My face against that man and against his family, and cut him off from among their people — him and all who go whoring after him, to whore after Molech.
And the person who turns to ghosts and to spirits, to whore after them — I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
And you shall set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
And you shall keep My statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.
The Penalties
Any man who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father and his mother; his blood is on him.
And a man who commits adultery with another man's wife — who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife — the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
And a man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood is on them.
And a man who lies with his daughter-in-law — both of them shall surely be put to death. They have done a mixing; their blood is on them.
And a man who lies with a male as one lies with a woman — both of them have done a detestable thing. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on them.
And a man who takes a woman and her mother — it is depravity. They shall burn him and them in the fire, so that there shall be no depravity among you.
And a man who gives his emission to an animal shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
And a woman who comes near any animal to mate with it — you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on them.

And a man who takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness — it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off in the sight of the sons of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he bears his guilt.

And a man who lies with a woman in her sickness and uncovers her nakedness — he has laid bare her source, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, because that is laying bare his own flesh. They shall bear their guilt.
And a man who lies with his uncle's wife has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They shall bear their sin; they shall die childless.
And a man who takes his brother's wife — it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They shall be childless.
Why You Are Not Like Them
And you shall keep all My statutes and all My judgments and do them, so that the land I am bringing you into to live in does not vomit you out.
And you shall not walk in the statutes of the nation I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was sick of them.

And I said to you: You shall take possession of their ground, and I will give it to you to possess — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

And you shall separate between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean, and you shall not make yourselves loathsome with any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, which I have separated out for you as unclean.
And you shall be holy to Me, because I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.
And a man or a woman who has a ghost or a spirit in them shall surely be put to death. They shall stone them with stones; their blood is on them."

chapters.title: Rules for the Priests
chapters.html:
Leviticus 21

A Priest and the Dead

1And the LORD said to Moses, "Say to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: None of them shall make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,

2except for his close flesh — for his mother and for his father, and for his son and for his daughter and for his brother,

3and for his unmarried sister, who is close to him because she has had no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.

4He shall not make himself unclean as a husband among his people, profaning himself.

5They shall not make a bald patch on their heads, and they shall not shave off the edge of their beards, and they shall not cut a gash in their flesh.

6They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God, because they present the offerings by fire of the LORD, the bread of their God. And they shall be holy.

7They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or who has been disgraced, and they shall not take a woman divorced from her husband, because he is holy to his God.

8And you shall treat him as holy, because he presents the bread of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD, who makes you holy, am holy.

9And a priest's daughter, if she profanes herself by prostituting herself, profanes her father. She shall be burned in the fire.

The High Priest

10And the priest who is greatest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and whose hand was filled to wear the garments, shall not let his hair go loose and shall not tear his clothes.

11And he shall not go in to any dead body. He shall not make himself unclean even for his father or for his mother.

12And he shall not go out of the sanctuary and profane the sanctuary of his God, because the crown of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.

13And he shall take a wife in her virginity.

14A widow, or a divorced woman, or a woman disgraced by prostitution — these he shall not take. He shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife,

15and he shall not profane his offspring among his people, because I am the LORD who makes him holy."

A Blemish

16And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

17"Speak to Aaron, saying: None of your offspring through their generations who has a blemish shall come near to present the bread of his God.

18No man at all who has a blemish shall come near: a man who is blind or lame, or disfigured in the face, or with a limb too long,

19or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,

20or a hunchback, or a withered man, or one with a spot in his eye, or a scab, or a skin eruption, or crushed testicles.

21No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come forward to present the offerings by fire of the LORD. He has a blemish; he shall not come forward to present the bread of his God.

22He may eat the bread of his God, from the most holy and from the holy.

23But he shall not come to the veil and shall not come near the altar, because he has a blemish, and he shall not profane My holy places, because I am the LORD who makes them holy."

24And Moses spoke this to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel.

Notes

  • vv1–3 the list of who a priest may bury — mother, father, son, daughter, brother, and an unmarried sister. A wife is not on the list. Whether she is covered by the obscure v4, or assumed under his close flesh in v2, or genuinely left out, has been argued for as long as the verse has existed, and the text does not resolve it.

  • v4 the broken verse — lo yittamma ba'al be-ammav le-hechallo, and it is one of the least recoverable sentences in Leviticus. Ba'al means a husband, an owner, a master; be-ammav is among his people; le-hechallo is to profane himself. The words are all ordinary and the sentence they make is not. It has been read as a rule about a priest's wife, about a chief among his kin, and as the conclusion of vv1–3. This rendering follows the words and leaves the difficulty where the Hebrew leaves it.

  • v5 the written and the spoken text — the consonants say yiqrechah, singular, and the reading tradition says yiqrechu, plural. It is one of only five places in Leviticus where the two part company; two of the others are Aaron's hand at 9:22 and at 16:21. Nothing turns on it here, which is itself worth seeing: these variants are usually this small.

  • v5 the same three mourning customs, again — a bald patch, a shaved beard-edge, a gash in the flesh. Two chapters ago the identical practices were forbidden to everyone (19:27–28). Here they are forbidden to priests specifically, in almost the same words. The Torah often legislates twice at two levels, and comparing the two tells you which audience each law was aimed at.

  • vv6, 8, 17, 21, 22 "the bread of their God" — lechem eloheihem, the same startling phrase as 3:11, where what goes up from the altar is called God's food. It is used five times in this chapter, always at the moment of saying what a priest is for: he is the one who brings God his bread. Nothing in these verses softens it.

  • v9 the priest's daughter — the harshest sentence in the chapter, and it falls on someone who is not a priest and cannot become one. The stated reason is entirely about her father: she profanes her father. Whatever holiness he carries is treated here as something her conduct can damage, and the penalty is the one given at 20:14 for depravity.

  • v10 "the priest who is greatest among his brothers" — ha-kohen ha-gadol, the great priest, which is where English gets high priest. Chapter 4 called the same office ha-kohen ha-mashiach, the anointed priest. Two titles for one man, and this one is about rank among his brothers rather than about oil.

  • vv10–11 forbidden to mourn at all — an ordinary priest may bury his own mother and father (v2). The high priest may not, and may not let his hair down or tear his clothes. That is exactly what Aaron and his surviving sons were forbidden at 10:6 on the day Nadab and Abihu died — the same two verbs. What was an emergency order in chapter 10 is written here as the permanent condition of the office.

  • vv18–20 the list nobody can fully translate — twelve conditions, and several of the words are effectively unknown. Tevallul occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in v20. Sarua occurs twice, both in Leviticus, and is usually taken as a limb of the wrong length. Charum is guessed from a root for cutting, so a damaged face. The English in every Bible is a reconstruction from roots and from the company the words keep, and the confident-sounding lists in modern translations are covering a good deal of uncertainty.

  • vv22–23 what he keeps — a priest with a blemish is not put out of the priesthood and not cut off from his family's living. He eats the holy food, including the most holy portions, which is the priests' sustenance and their inheritance in place of land. What he cannot do is approach the altar or the veil. The distinction the chapter draws is between being a priest and performing at the altar, and it draws it in two verses without explanation.
